content: Logan College of Chiropractic, a private institution established in 1935, is located in Chesterfield, Missouri, near St. Louis. The college offers degree programs in Chiropractic, Pre-Chiropractic, Sport Science, and Rehabilitation. The current president of the university is Dr. George A. C. Dr. Goodman, who was appointed as the president of Logan in 1993. Logan College of Chiropractic, originally known as Logan Basic College of Chiropractic, was named after its founder and first president, Hugh B. C. Logan. The college enrolled its inaugural class of seven men and women on September 1, 1935. Initially, the institution operated out of a converted residence located at 4490 Lindell Boulevard in St. Louis. Later, the college relocated to a 17-acre estate in the suburb of St. Louis called Normandy. In the summer of 1973, Logan College moved to its current location, which was formerly a Maryknoll Seminary, situated on a wooded hilltop in Chesterfield, Missouri. In 1987, the North Central Association granted accreditation to Logan College for its academic programs. Since then, Logan has maintained continuous reaccreditation from both the North Central Association and other accrediting organizations. Logan College offers four degree programs: Doctor of Chiropractic, Master of Science in Sport Science and Rehabilitation, and Bachelor of Science degrees in Human Biology and Life Sciences. Admission to the Doctor of Chiropractic (DC) program requires a minimum of 90 semester hours (equivalent to 135 quarter hours) of undergraduate coursework, which is approximately three years of collegiate study. Specific entrance requirements include six semester hours (or nine quarter hours) each in Biological Sciences, Inorganic (General) Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, and Physics, all with appropriate laboratory components. Additionally, students must complete 15 semester hours (or 22.5 quarter hours) in Humanities or Social Sciences. The Doctor of Chiropractic program spans 10 trimesters, equivalent to 3⅓ years. For the Master of Science in Sport Science and Rehabilitation program, prerequisites include a bachelor’s degree and certain science coursework. This program is five trimesters in length. Logan College merged with Carver Chiropractic College in Oklahoma City in 1958 and with Missouri College of Chiropractic in 1964.
